policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'in a little foolishness' renders the quantifier once; the indefinite τι adds nothing English marks apart from μικρόν, so the ASV cannot show whether it stood.

ASV makes 'foolishness' the thing borne a little of — 'bear with me in a little foolishness' — which is the partitive genitive μικρόν τι ἀφροσύνης. The dative τῇ ἀφροσύνῃ leaves μικρόν adverbial ('bear with me a little in my folly', as KJV renders it), a construction the ASV does not have. The note is an alternative_rendering of ἀνέχεσθε and does not bear on this unit.
Pure word order between verb and object; 'the serpent beguiled Eve' is the only English order either Greek sequence yields.

ASV has no correlative in the apodosis: 'as the serpent beguiled Eve ... your minds should be corrupted.' οὕτως would be rendered 'so' answering the preceding ὡς, and the ASV renders such correlatives elsewhere rather than dropping them.
ASV renders both nouns: 'from the simplicity and the purity that is toward Christ.' 'and the purity' is καὶ τῆς ἁγνότητος, absent from the omitting reading.

ASV 'ye do well to bear with him' is present indicative. The augmented forms are imperfect and give the past/potential sense KJV carried ('ye might well bear with him'); the ASV's change to the present marks ἀνέχεσθε.

ASV is active with Paul as agent: 'have we made this manifest unto you.' φανερωθέντες is passive ('having been made manifest'), which the ASV nowhere reflects; the note offers only an alternative English wording of the same active clause.
Word order of reflexive and pronoun only; 'I kept myself from being burdensome unto you' follows from either sequence.
ASV 'And no marvel' does not distinguish the noun from the adjective: KJV renders the adjectival reading θαυμαστόν with the same English phrase, so the wording is neutral between them.
Word order only; 'I speak not after the Lord' is the English of either sequence.
Presence of the article with σάρκα; 'after the flesh' is the ASV's rendering of the anarthrous and articular alike, so the English cannot show it.
Word order of object and prepositional phrase; 'if he smiteth you on the face' follows from either sequence.
Perfect against aorist of the same verb; ASV's 'as though we had been weak' inside the ὡς ὅτι clause suits either tense in English.

ASV lists prisons before stripes — 'in prisons more abundantly, in stripes above measure' — which excludes the transposed order of r02. The remaining two readings differ only in spacing before the comma and are indistinguishable in English.
Repetition of the preposition before κόπῳ; the ASV supplies 'in' at the head of each item of the list regardless, so the English does not show whether ἐν stood here.

ASV 'that which presseth upon me daily' renders the sense of pressure in ἐπίστασις. ἐπισύστασις is a crowding or concourse, which KJV rendered 'that which cometh upon me daily'; the ASV's change to 'presseth' marks the shorter word. The notes concern παρεκτός, not this unit.
Dative against genitive of the pronoun. 'Presseth upon me' fits the dative, but the genitive ('my daily pressure') is also rendered 'upon me' in English — KJV does so — so the ASV does not settle it.
ASV has 'of the Lord Jesus' with no 'Christ'; the added Χριστοῦ would appear in the English name. The notes concern the rendering of θεὸς καὶ πατήρ and of εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας.
Word order of noun and genitive; 'the city of the Damascenes' is the English of either sequence.
ASV reads 'in order to take me' with no verb of wishing; θέλων would be rendered 'desiring/willing to take me' as KJV has it.
